newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela mulls deportation of Basque separatist.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela mulls deportation of Basque separatist.

text.p: The Venezuelan government said on Thursday it would deport a Basque separatist if the country's Supreme Court refused to extradite him to Spain.
"If he is not extradited, Venezuela will deport him, but not to Spain," Interior Minister Jose Guillermo Andueza told reporters at the Miraflores presidential palace.
Ramon Sagarzazu handed himself over to Venezuelan authorities a week ago when he arrived in the South American country without a passport seeking political asylum. Spain is seeking his extradition.
Andueza said Sagarzazu, a member of the Basque separatist group ETA since 1986, was being held while the Supreme Court considered Spain's extradition request.
"We think we will have a decision from the court in a month or month and a half," he said.
In a letter directed to Andueza and Venezuela's Congress published in local newspapers on Thursday, Sagarzazu pleaded with Venezuelan authorities not to send him back to Spain.
Sagarzazu said his life was in danger there due to his political beliefs.
The murder by ETA guerrillas of a young town councilor in northern Spain on July 10 has sparked a wave of popular outrage against the group.
Andueza said 25 other known ETA members who have lived in Venezuela for more than a decade are not under arrest but are required to report to police periodically.
"Up to now they have carried out legitimate activities in the country," he said.
ETA began its armed campaign for an independent state in 1968 and has since carried out frequent of attacks on Spanish political targets.
